priorityReason: Nothing academic can exist without it. Students, staff, attendance, timetable and results all attach to a class.

goal.capability: to create the classes for an academic session and set each one as Fixed or Subject Wise
goal.outcome: every other module has a known class to attach to, structured the way the school actually teaches it

dataFields.name: Class name
dataFields.validation: 2 to 60 characters. Unique within the academic session and branch (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Class order
dataFields.validation: Where the class sits in the school's sequence, so lists and promotion read in the right order rather than alphabetically.

dataFields.name: Academic session
dataFields.validation: The session the class belongs to. Not changeable after creation (BR-2).

dataFields.name: Class type
dataFields.validation: Fixed means every student takes the same subjects. Subject Wise means students take a selection, which changes how fees, timetable and results are calculated (BR-4).

dataFields.name: Subjects
dataFields.validation: The subjects the class carries. At least one is required, and a Subject Wise class marks which are compulsory (BR-5).

dataFields.name: Compulsory
dataFields.validation: Per subject. Only meaningful for a Subject Wise class, where an optional subject is one a student may not take.
dataFields.requiredWhen: The class type is Subject Wise

dataFields.name: Age range
dataFields.validation: The ages the class normally takes, used to check an inquiry at the point it is submitted.

businessRules.rule: A class must exist before anything can attach to it. Sections, students, attendance, timetable, assignments and results all key off it.
A class belongs to one academic session. Creating next session's classes does not disturb this session's, and a class is never carried between sessions by editing its session.
A class name is unique within its academic session and branch. Two classes called Grade 4 in one session make every list ambiguous.

The class type decides how the class is treated everywhere. Fixed means every student takes the same subjects; Subject Wise means students take a selection, which changes how fees, timetable and results are calculated.
A class carries at least one subject. A class with no subjects cannot be timetabled, taught or examined.
The class type cannot be changed once students are placed in any of its sections. Changing it would alter how their fees and results are calculated part way through a session.
A subject cannot be removed from a class once marks, a timetable slot or an assignment exists against it in that session. Removing it would orphan work already done.
A change to a class is reflected everywhere the class is used, in the same request. A register printed after a name correction shows the corrected name.
A class is deactivated, never deleted, and cannot be deactivated at all while it holds an active section or a placed student.
Creating a class creates no sections and no students. It is a structure, and students are placed into sections rather than into classes.

transitions.condition: No active section and no placed student remain (BR-9).
The class is reinstated within the same session.

basicFlow.userAction: Opens Class and Session and starts a new class for the academic session.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Loads the form scoped to the current open academic session.

basicFlow.navigation: Create class → Name, order and type
basicFlow.userAction: Enters the class name and its order, and sets the type as Fixed or Subject Wise.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks the name is unique within the session and branch.

basicFlow.userAction: Attaches the subjects the class carries, marking which are compulsory where the class is Subject Wise.

basicFlow.systemResponse: Creates the class for that academic session and makes it available for sections to be created under it.
Makes the class readable by the attendance, timetable, assignment and examination modules, which become available for it.

basicFlow.userAction: Changes the class later where the school's structure changes.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Refuses a type change where students are already placed, and refuses removing a subject that already carries marks, a timetable slot or an assignment.

alternateFlows.behaviour: Each subject is marked compulsory or optional, since a student in a Subject Wise class takes a selection rather than all of them. This is what fees, timetable and results read afterwards (BR-4).

alternateFlows.condition: A new academic session is being set up
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Class & Session → Academic session → Create class
alternateFlows.behaviour: The classes are created afresh against the new session. This session's classes are untouched and keep their students (BR-2).

alternateFlows.condition: A subject is added to a class mid-session
alternateFlows.behaviour: The subject becomes available to every section of that class, and to the timetable and examination modules from that point on.

alternateFlows.condition: A class is no longer run
alternateFlows.behaviour: The class is deactivated only once no active section and no placed student remain. It stays readable in historical reports (BR-9).

openQuestions.question: Are classes carried forward when a new academic session opens, or created afresh each time?
openQuestions.assumption: Created afresh. A copy-forward tool would help but is not specified.

openQuestions.question: Who maintains the subject list — School Admin or Coordinator?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified here. It sits with curriculum management.

openQuestions.question: Should the age range on a class be enforced at admission, or only warned about?
openQuestions.assumption: It is checked on the inquiry form, which rejects an out-of-range date of birth.

openQuestions.question: Can two branches of the same school have differently structured classes of the same name?
openQuestions.assumption: Yes. A class is scoped to a branch and a session.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
